Who we are
The City of Salisbury is the most progressive council in South Australia, driving growth, jobs, housing and opportunity in the north. With a workforce of over 400 people, we offer the chance to collaborate with teams across the organisation to deliver meaningful, community-focused projects.
The City Infrastructure Department delivers asset management, capital works, and maintenance programs, as well as oversees lease management for local community and sporting clubs, and security and civil compliance functions.
Join us and see the positive impact your work can make.
About the role
The City of Salisbury is seeking three experienced Asset Engineers to join the Engineering Assets & Systems team within City Infrastructure. Opportunities are available across Civil, Roads and Drainage asset portfolios.
Reporting to the Divisional Head, Engineering Assets & Systems (Asset Engineer - Civil and Asset Engineer - Roads) or the Senior Stormwater Engineer (Asset Engineer - Drainage), you will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving asset management plans, undertaking engineering investigations and modelling, and supporting long-term infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
You will play a key role in managing and improving some of the City's most important infrastructure assets, including roads, drainage networks, wetlands, bridges, boardwalks, coastal assets, carparks, signage and stormwater infrastructure, helping ensure they continue to meet the needs of our growing community.
Your key responsibilities will include
- Develop, maintain and improve Asset Management Plans across a range of infrastructure asset classes.
- Undertake engineering investigations, modelling, analysis and reporting to support asset management decisions.
- Develop capital renewal, maintenance and lifecycle programs.
- Assess asset condition, risk, service levels and long-term investment priorities.
- Prepare project briefs and business cases for infrastructure projects and renewal programs.
- Evaluate consultant reports, designs and technical proposals.
- Provide specialist engineering and asset management advice across the organisation.
- Support planning for future growth and infrastructure needs across the city.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community members, developers, government agencies, service authorities and internal stakeholders.
- Communicate technical information and asset management recommendations clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders, including residents, elected members and senior leaders.
- Respond to enquiries from residents, elected members and other stakeholders.
About you
You are a qualified engineer with experience in infrastructure asset management and a passion for delivering practical, long-term outcomes for communities. You combine strong technical capability with excellent communication skills and can confidently engage with a wide range of stakeholders. You are able to translate complex engineering and asset management information into clear, practical advice that supports informed decision-making.
You will also have
- Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, equivalent qualifications, or proven extensive experience in asset management relating to civil infrastructure and stormwater.
- Experience in infrastructure asset management, planning and lifecycle analysis.
- Knowledge of asset management frameworks such as ISO 55000 and IIMM/IPWEA practices.
- Experience using asset management, GIS and engineering modelling systems.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven experience building productive relationships with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong written communication skills, including the preparation of reports, business cases and technical documentation.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable
- Postgraduate qualifications in asset management.
- Experience working within local government.
What we offer
- State-of-the-art Salisbury Community Hub is 25 minutes from the CBD with excellent rail and road connections.
- Modern and positive work environments.
- Free car parking.
- Flexible work options.
- Three additional leave days per year.
- Annual pay rises.
- Health and wellbeing programs, including skin checks, health assessments, flu vaccinations and an employee assistance program.
- Professional development opportunities.

- Learn directly from experienced engineers through supervised assignments, regular feedback and technical review.

Work closely with experienced engineer professionals and project management teams.

Be part of a growing business with ongoing residential construction and development projects.

candidates.abstract: Draft diverse civil and structural projects from design through to fabrication and construction with an established WA contractor.
bullets: Civil, structural and fabrication drafting
Diverse specialist construction projects
Work closely with engineering and site teams
candidates.content_text:
We are currently seeking an experienced Civil / Structural Draftsperson to join a well-established WA contractor delivering specialist construction projects across the commercial, civil, infrastructure and resources sectors.
This is a great opportunity for a practical Draftsperson who enjoys working across a diverse range of projects involving structural steel, fabricated components, concrete works, civil construction and specialist infrastructure.
Working closely with Project Managers, Engineers and site teams, you will be responsible for producing accurate drawings and documentation that can be effectively taken from design through to fabrication and construction.
What's in it for you?
 - Permanent opportunity with an established WA construction contractor
 - Diverse project exposure across civil, structural and specialist construction
 - Work closely with experienced Project Managers, Engineers and site personnel
 - Varied role with involvement from initial design through to construction
 - South of the river location
 Your responsibilities will include:
 - Producing detailed construction, fabrication and shop drawings
 - Preparing drawings for structural steel, gates, fencing systems and associated fabricated components
 - Drafting concrete footings, plinths, foundations and other structural elements
 - Assisting with drawings for civil works, underground services and associated infrastructure
 - Reviewing engineering and construction drawings, specifications and project documentation
 - Updating and revising drawings throughout the project lifecycle
 - Preparing as-built drawings and maintaining accurate drawing registers
 - Liaising with Project Managers, Engineers, workshop personnel and site teams
 - Working from site measurements, engineering designs and client specifications
 - Identifying potential constructability issues and working with the project team to develop practical solutions
 - Ensuring drawings meet project requirements, relevant standards and client specifications
 To be successful in this role, you will ideally have:
 - Previous experience working as a Draftsperson within construction, structural steel, civil, fabrication or a similar environment
 - Strong experience using AutoCAD or similar drafting software
 - Ability to read and interpret engineering and construction drawings
 - Understanding of structural steel, fabricated components, concrete or civil construction
 - Strong attention to detail and accuracy
 - Good communication skills with the ability to work alongside both office and site-based teams
 - Ability to manage drawing revisions and multiple project requirements
 - A practical understanding of how drawings translate into fabrication and construction
 A qualification in Drafting, Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering or a related discipline will be highly regarded.
Candidates with experience in structural steel fabrication, civil construction, concrete, security infrastructure, gates or specialist construction projects are strongly encouraged to apply.
Apply Now
 If you are an experienced Draftsperson looking for a varied role where you can work across design, fabrication and construction, we want to hear from you.
 Apply now with an updated resume to discuss the opportunity further.

candidates.content_text:
Cadet Designer
Requisition Number: 1400
Salary Range: $64,175.57 - $86,649.77 per annum
Position Type: Full Time Maximum Term for up to 6 Years
Cadet Position – This position is intended for up to a 6-year maximum term to allow for 2 years of bonded service to Council post-graduation.
Location: Council Chambers, 119-145 Spence Street, Cairns
Application Close Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 11.30pm AEST
Kick-start your career in Civil Design with one of the region’s largest and most diverse infrastructure portfolios!
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Cadet Designer to join our Design & Survey Services team. This is an exciting opportunity to earn while you learn, gain hands-on industry experience, and build a rewarding career in civil engineering and infrastructure design.
Our Ideal Candidate:
We are seeking a Cadet Designer who is eager to learn and willing to dedicate themselves to continuous development within a technically focused environment. The ideal candidate will have completed Year 12 or hold a Certificate III in Engineering and be qualified for acceptance into an Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil) course, or an equivalent qualification. They will demonstrate a detail-oriented mindset, strong analytical skills, and a willingness to integrate into and contribute positively to the established team culture. A current "C" Class Driver's Licence is required, with the ability to independently drive between business locations to meet operational needs. The successful candidate will also maintain a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes for the Cairns community.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Undertake training in the use of civil design software (AutoCAD, 12d Model and relevant GIS systems).
- Undertake training in the investigation, planning, development and delivery of civil design projects.
- Develop knowledge and understanding of relevant standards, guidelines and legislative documents (e.g. Austroads, Queensland Urban Drainage Manual, Queensland Streets, Main Roads technical publications and Australian Standards).
- Assist with field investigations, traffic surveys and stakeholder consultation associated with allocated projects.
- Preparation of detailed civil design drawings and estimates for a range of multi-disciplinary infrastructure projects with guidance and as directed.
- Provide general administrative assistance such as database maintenance and document control using established procedures.
- Develop an approach to contributing technical knowledge and innovative problem solutions to design activities.
Study Allowances
Council provides paid study and examination leave, along with course fee reimbursements, to support your professional development and ensure success in your university studies.
Why Join the Design Team?
Supportive Team Environment
Our team combines professionalism with a relaxed and supportive culture. We value collaboration, open communication, and the occasional good-natured banter. We pride ourselves on fostering an environment where people can enjoy coming to work and working together to achieve quality outcomes.
Professional Growth and Development
The team provides excellent opportunities for learning and career development. Graduates, cadets and even experienced professionals benefit from mentorship, knowledge sharing and support from highly experienced staff.
Unique Lifestyle Benefits
Based in Cairns, we benefit from the unique lifestyle provided by the area. Nestled between the reef and rainforest, the region offers an abundance of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors and maintain a healthy work-life balance.
Diverse and Meaningful Projects
Our project portfolio is varied and challenging, providing opportunities to work across multiple disciplines and asset types. No two projects are the same, and team members take pride in delivering infrastructure that benefits the local community.
Some benefits we offer:
- Achieve work / life balance with flexible working arrangements
- Fitness Passport - subsidised health and well-being memberships (gym/swimming pool)
- Recharge with up to 5 weeks annual leave
- Up to 3 weeks personal leave
- Cherish family time with up to 14 weeks paid parental leave
- Grow personally and professionally with learning and development opportunities
- Salary sacrifice opportunities
- Up to $5,000 study assistance per annum (inclusive of Fringe Benefits Tax) towards the cost of your Associate Degree in Engineering (Civil)
We are committed to:
- Fostering a collaborative and inclusive work environment
- Embracing innovation and continuous improvement
- Cultivating a culture of professional growth and support
Now we want to hear about YOU!
Applications MUST be submitted online through the 'Apply' button and include a Cover Letter addressing the selection criteria and Resume outlining previous academic and work experience and if requested include attachments of the relevant qualifications and licenses, relating to the role.
For further information about this role please download the Position Description which includes the Key Duties, Responsibilities and Selection Criteria.

Phone: (07) 4044 3310
Email: jobs@cairns.qld.gov.au

candidates.abstract: Help shape safer, stronger transport infrastructure while building your civil engineering career with TMR.

candidates.content_text:
Build infrastructure that keeps Queensland moving!
Are you a civil engineer ready to apply your technical knowledge to meaningful transport projects? Join Transport and Main Roads and help plan, deliver and manage roads, bridges and other infrastructure that support safe and reliable travel across Central Queensland.
About the role
As a Civil Engineer, you will work with experienced engineering and project professionals across the full project lifecycle. You will contribute to transport planning, project development, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management activities, while building your capability under the guidance of senior engineering staff.
Central Queensland Region manages transport infrastructure across more than 600,000 square kilometres, including over 9,000 kilometres of state-controlled roads and 1,500 kilometres of the National Land Transport Network. With offices in Rockhampton, Mackay, Emerald and Barcaldine, the region offers exposure to varied infrastructure, environments and engineering challenges.
In this role, you will:
* provide technical engineering advice and undertake assessments to support planning, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management
* manage projects or project components to achieve quality outcomes, value for money and sound engineering practice
* identify project risks, emerging issues and opportunities, and develop practical and cost-effective solutions
* support procurement activities and the administration of consultant and construction contracts
* coordinate budgets, forecasting, accruals, procurement and performance reporting
* contribute to the delivery of road, bridge, maintenance and asset improvement projects
* build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders
* ensure work meets relevant governance, safety, risk management and departmental requirements.
What you will bring
You will use sound judgement, take responsibility for the quality of your work and collaborate effectively to achieve project outcomes. You will be comfortable applying civil engineering and project management principles across multiple infrastructure projects, while actively developing your professional knowledge and capability.
You must hold:
* a four-year Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering, or an equivalent qualification accepted by Engineers Australia
* a current Class C driver licence.
Why join TMR?
You will gain hands-on experience across diverse transport infrastructure projects while working alongside experienced professionals. TMR supports career development, an inclusive workplace and a healthy work-life balance.
This role provides an opportunity to strengthen your technical, project management, commercial and stakeholder engagement skills while contributing to infrastructure that makes a practical difference for Queensland communities.
If you are looking for varied civil engineering work, professional support and the opportunity to contribute across the full project lifecycle, we encourage you to apply.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.             
Job Ad Reference: QLD/707063/26
Closing Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026

candidates.content_text:
The UGL Utilities team designs, constructs and maintains critical infrastructure across the water and power sectors. Ranging from wastewater treatment plants to power stations. We design and construct the following assets; power generation, transmission lines, substations, electrical distribution networks, water and wastewater treatment plans and water pipelines.
 Our Utilities team works hard and celebrates successes and efforts. If you are looking for a bright future and opportunity to grow your career, then join UGL – a great place to work!
 The Opportunity
 UGL Utilities team are currently looking for an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join the team in Perth. This role requires DIDO to the project site in Narrogin on a 2:1 roster.  
 Key Responsibilities 
 - Develop and implement detailed project plans, work schedules, and methodologies for civil works, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets and scope.
 - Review and interpret technical drawings, specifications, and contracts; provide engineering input to ensure compliance with industry standards, UGL requirements, and client expectations.
 - Oversee on-site civil construction activities, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and to the requires quality standards; manage subcontractor performance and resolve site issues as they arise.
 - Promote and enforce UGL’s HSE policies and procedures across all civil project activities; ensure risk assessments and safety measures are effectively implemented.
 - Liase with clients, internal teams, and external stakeholders to provide regular updates. Manage expectations, and address engineering or construction challenges; prepare and deliver progress reports and technical documentation.
 About you
 - Tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering or a related discipline, with eligibility for membership with Engineers Australia (or equivalent).
 - Proven experience delivering civil engineering works in infrastructure, utilities, or construction projects – ideally within a multi-disciplinary or contractor environment.
 - Strong understanding of civil design principles, construction methodologies, and relevant Australian standards, with the ability to interpret drawings and technical documentation.
 - Demonstrated commitment to health, safety, environmental, and quality standards, with experience implementing and maintaining compliance on project sites.
 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with internal teams, client and subcontractors to achieve project outcomes.
 What makes you right for UGL 
 - Ability to provide a safe, supportive, and positive workplace. 
 - Empower a united and collaborative culture.
 - Deliver technical excellence and create efficient, innovative solutions.
 - Build an enviable reputation and the trust of employees, clients, and other stakeholders.
 - Genuine concern for safety.
 About Us   
 UGL is well-known and respected for providing end-to-end engineering, construction and maintenance services within, rai and transport, communications and technology systems, oil and gas, power, renewables and resources, water and defence markets. UGL partners with some of the world’s largest blue-chip companies and government agencies, private enterprises, and public institutions. We are a member of the CIMIC Group of companies.
 At UGL, we value diversity – in the backgrounds, ideas, work styles and perspectives of our team. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and strongly encourage people with disability, Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander people, mature aged workers, and people from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply. 
 Please note that relevant screening checks will be conducted as part of the recruitment process. These may include a national criminal history check and for you to undergo pre-employment medical assessment including drug and alcohol screen. 
 UGL does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or recruitment agencies.

candidates.content_text:
My client is seeking an experienced Civil Project Engineer to join the project team delivering works on the Pilbara Port of Ashburton Foundations and Firewater Installation Project.
 This is an excellent opportunity for a Civil Project Engineer to secure an immediate start on a three-month FIFO contract, contributing to the delivery of a range of civil infrastructure, foundations and services installation packages.
 The successful candidate will play an integral role in coordinating construction activities, managing subcontractors and ensuring project works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with programme, budget and quality requirements.
On Offer
 - Role: Civil Project Engineer
 - Project: Pilbara Port of Ashburton – Foundations and Firewater Installation
 - Location: Onslow, Western Australia
 - Duration: 3 months
 - Start Date: Immediate 
 - Rate: $87 per hour + superannuation
 - Payment: Weekly
 - Roster: 2:1 FIFO from Perth
 - Hours: 12 hours per day
 - Shift: 6:00am – 6:00pm
 - Flights: Friday afternoon departures from Perth
 Project Scope 
The successful candidate will be involved in the coordination and delivery of multiple civil construction and infrastructure packages, including:
 - Stormwater drainage installation and associated underground services.
 - Coordination and management of in-situ services.
 - Firewater and potable water pipeline installation.
 - Electrical services trenching and installation.
 - Tank foundations and associated infrastructure installation.
 - Soft and hard landscaping works.
 - Road construction and associated civil infrastructure.
 - General earthworks, concrete and foundation works.
 Key Responsibilities 
Reporting to the Project Manager and working closely with the site construction team, your responsibilities will include:
 - Coordinating and managing day-to-day civil construction activities across multiple work fronts.
 - Planning and overseeing the delivery of civil infrastructure, earthworks, concrete, foundations and underground services packages.
 - Managing subcontractors, suppliers, labour resources and plant to ensure works are completed safely and efficiently.
 - Developing and maintaining construction programmes, short-term lookaheads and daily work plans.
 - Monitoring construction progress against project milestones, identifying potential delays and implementing corrective actions.
 - Reviewing and interpreting construction drawings, technical specifications, scopes of work and engineering documentation.
 - Coordinating the installation of stormwater drainage, firewater, potable water and electrical services.
 - Overseeing quality assurance activities, including ITPs, inspections, test records and quality documentation.
 - Ensuring construction activities comply with project specifications, approved methodologies and relevant Australian Standards.
 - Monitoring project costs, variations, productivity and resource utilisation.
 Skills & Experience 
To be considered for this opportunity, you will ideally demonstrate:
 - A minimum of 5 years' experience in civil construction project engineering and delivery.
 - A Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) – mandatory.
 - Strong practical knowledge of concrete, foundations, earthworks and general civil construction.
 - Demonstrated experience coordinating civil infrastructure and underground services installation.
 - Previous experience managing subcontractors and coordinating multiple construction work fronts.
 - The ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and construction documentation.
 - Experience with quality assurance processes, ITPs, inspections and project reporting.
 - Strong communication, planning and organisational skills.
 - The ability to work autonomously in a remote construction environment and contribute effectively to the wider project team.
 Mandatory Requirements 
Candidates must hold or be able to provide:
 - Bachelor of Engineering (Civil).
 - Current White Card.
 - Current driver's licence.
 - Australian working rights.
 - Ability to provide 100 points of identification.

We are certified to international standards for quality, safety and the environment. We strive for improved project efficiency through the use of technology that ultimately helps us reduce costs and reduce our impact on the environment.
Our Estimators are responsible for the preparation of all project estimates and corresponding documentation in a timely and efficient manner.
Duties include
- Review various tender sites and identify those civil works and earthworks tenders that have been released for pricing.
- Drawing upon technical knowledge and industry experience, prepare comprehensive costing schedules by referring to technical drawings, scoping documents, client contracts and company resources.
- Use a variety of software packages for undertaking accurate costings.
- Prepare and submit tender documentation to clients and undertake negotiations within established parameters to win projects.
- Prepare comprehensive project handover notes and files.
- A positive "can do" attitude with high client servicing standards.
- Awareness of technical standards and regulatory requirements and the impact on project costs.
- Consideration of Safety, Quality and Environmental management principles on projects.  
Requirements
- The ability to interpret working drawings, scoping documents and tender contracts, and, translate these into accurate and thorough project estimates is essential.
- A strong background and experience (3 years) in civil works and earthworks projects and or estimation is a key requirement of the position.
- The ability to prioritize and manage high work volume and at times willing to work outside of normal business hours is expected and reflected in the remuneration package.
- A strong understanding of IT and various software packages such as the Microsoft suite. Specific technical software such as Expert Estimation and Mudshark is desirable.
- Proficient in English written and verbal skills is essential.
- Well-developed interpersonal skills with the ability to convey complex technical data in a simplistic and logical manner is highly sort after.
If you’re a proactive Estimator looking to take ownership of projects and work with a company that values our team, quality and experience, we’d like to hear from you – Apply Now

candidates.content_text:
Estimator - Civil Construction
 Location: Northern Suburbs, Perth WA
Salary: $140,000 - $180,000 + Super (negotiable for the right candidate)
Employment: Permanent, Full-Time
Hours: Monday - Friday, 38 hours per week
Working Arrangements: Flexible working arrangements
 The Opportunity
 An established civil construction contractor is seeking an Estimator to join its growing pre-contracts team, based at its northern suburbs head office.
 This is an excellent opportunity for an Estimator with 2-5 years' experience in civil construction who is looking to further develop their technical and commercial capabilities within an established contractor.
 Working across a variety of civil engineering tenders, you will be involved in preparing first-principles estimates, developing tender submissions and working closely with internal project teams, clients, suppliers and subcontractors to deliver competitive and commercially sound bids.
 You'll also have the opportunity to work alongside experienced senior estimating professionals, gaining exposure to larger and more complex civil construction projects while developing your career.
 Key Responsibilities
 - Prepare accurate and competitive first-principles estimates for small to medium-sized civil construction tenders.
 - Coordinate the preparation of tender submissions from initial pricing and bid strategy through to final submission.
 - Review drawings, specifications, scopes of work and project requirements to establish accurate project costs.
 - Obtain and assess pricing from suppliers and subcontractors.
 - Identify commercial risks, opportunities and potential cost-saving initiatives.
 - Assist with tender strategy development, programming and cost analysis.
 - Work collaboratively with Quantity Schedulers, Project Managers and other internal stakeholders.
 - Build and maintain effective relationships with clients, consultants, suppliers and subcontractors.
 - Identify opportunities to improve estimating processes, programming and risk management methodologies.
 About You
 - A Bachelor of Civil Engineering (mandatory).
 - Approximately 2-5 years' estimating experience within the civil construction industry.
 - At least two years of on-site project experience.
 - A sound understanding of civil construction methodologies, programming and scheduling.
 - Experience preparing first-principles estimates and tender submissions.
 - Strong commercial awareness and an understanding of construction costs.
 - Experience engaging with clients, consultants, suppliers and subcontractors.
 - High proficiency in Expert Estimation.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office and MS Project.
 - Strong communication, organisational and problem-solving skills.
 You must also hold unrestricted Australian working rights, a current driver's licence and be able to obtain and maintain a National Police Clearance.
 What's on Offer?
 - Salary between $140,000 - $180,000 + Super, with flexibility for exceptional candidates.
 - Permanent, full-time opportunity.
 - Flexible working arrangements and hours.
 - Convenient northern suburbs office location.
 - Exposure to a diverse range of civil construction tenders.
 - Opportunity to work alongside experienced Senior Estimators and develop your career.
 - A supportive and collaborative working environment.
 Working Hours: Monday to Friday, generally between 8am and 5pm, with flexibility around start and finish times. Some additional hours may be required to meet critical tender submission deadlines.
 Apply Now
 If you're an Estimator with a civil construction background looking for your next career opportunity, we'd welcome your application.
 For a confidential discussion, please contact:
chris.wright@cgcrecruitment.com
